fields.description: Rich culture of Punjab
fields.cultural_summary: Summary

fields.name: Rajasthan
fields.description: The land of royalty, desert dunes, grand forts, vibrant folk music, and colourful tapestries.
fields.cultural_summary: Rajasthan is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Kerala
fields.description: God's Own Country, famed for its lush backwaters, Kathakali theatrics, Ayurvedic traditions, and fragrant spice plantations.
fields.cultural_summary: Kerala is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Tamil Nadu
fields.description: The land of ancient Dravidian temples, Bharatanatyam precision, Carnatic music ragas, and classical Tamil literature.
fields.cultural_summary: Tamil Nadu is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Gujarat
fields.description: The land of vibrant textiles, coastal trade, festive Garba nights, architectural stepwells, and hospitable merchant traditions.
fields.cultural_summary: Gujarat is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Maharashtra
fields.description: The land of Maratha warriors, Sahyadri fortresses, saintly Varkari traditions, Bollywood glamour, and dynamic festivities.
fields.cultural_summary: Maharashtra is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: West Bengal
fields.description: The cultural hub of art, Nobel literature, terracotta temples, riverine mangrove forests, and soul-stirring Baul philosophy.
fields.cultural_summary: West Bengal is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Odisha
fields.description: The soul of temple architecture, Odissi classical grace, sacred Jagannath customs, and ancient maritime trade heritage.
fields.cultural_summary: Odisha is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Assam
fields.description: Gateway to Northeast India, blessed with the mighty Brahmaputra, one-horned rhinos, emerald tea hills, and golden Muga silk.
fields.cultural_summary: Assam is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Manipur
fields.description: The jewel of India, famed for classical Raas Leela grace, Loktak floating lake, indigenous polo (Sagol Kangjei), and martial arts.
fields.cultural_summary: Manipur is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Karnataka
fields.description: The land of Vijayanagara ruins at Hampi, fragrant sandalwood forests, coffee plantations of Coorg, and tech innovation in Bengaluru.
fields.cultural_summary: Karnataka is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Andhra Pradesh
fields.description: The land of Tirupati hills, Kuchipudi classical drama, Kalamkari textiles, and fiery coastal spice gastronomy.
fields.cultural_summary: Andhra Pradesh is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Telangana
fields.description: The land of the Kakatiya dynasty, Golconda diamonds, Charminar bazaars, Bathukamma flowers, and vibrant Deccan heritage.
fields.cultural_summary: Telangana is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Uttar Pradesh
fields.description: The cradle of Indian civilization along the Ganga and Yamuna, home to Kashi's ghats, Awadhi courts, and the Taj Mahal.
fields.cultural_summary: Uttar Pradesh is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Madhya Pradesh
fields.description: The heart of incredible India, renowned for Khajuraho temples, Sanchi stupas, tiger reserves, and tribal Gond artistry.
fields.cultural_summary: Madhya Pradesh is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Chhattisgarh
fields.description: The land of pristine Sal forests, Chitrakote "Niagara" falls, Bastar bell-metal craftsmanship, and Pandavani epics.
fields.cultural_summary: Chhattisgarh is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Bihar
fields.description: The historic land of the Buddha's enlightenment, Mahavira, ancient Nalanda University, and vibrant Madhubani painting.
fields.cultural_summary: Bihar is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Jharkhand
fields.description: The land of dense forests, cascading waterfalls, rich minerals, tribal Santhal traditions, and Birsa Munda's courage.
fields.cultural_summary: Jharkhand is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Himachal Pradesh
fields.description: The land of snow-clad peaks, apple valleys, pine forests, ancient wooden temples, and peaceful mountain shrines.
fields.cultural_summary: Himachal Pradesh is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Uttarakhand
fields.description: Devbhoomi, the Land of the Gods, cradle of the Ganges, snow-clad Garhwal and Kumaon ranges, and sacred Char Dham shrines.
fields.cultural_summary: Uttarakhand is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Haryana
fields.description: The land of the historic Kurukshetra battlefield, ancient Saraswati civilization, robust wrestling traditions, and fertile green fields.
fields.cultural_summary: Haryana is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Sikkim
fields.description: The Himalayan paradise nestled under Mount Kanchenjunga, India's first 100% organic state, famed for orchid blooms and Buddhist monasteries.
fields.cultural_summary: Sikkim is renowned for its iconic heritage, artistic traditions, vibrant festivals, and unique gastronomy.

fields.name: Arunachal Pradesh
fields.description: The Land of Dawn-Lit Mountains, Arunachal Pradesh is a biodiversity hotspot and a cradle of diverse indigenous tribes, Theravada and Mahayana Buddhist monasteries, and vibrant animist folklore.
fields.cultural_summary: Rich in tribal heritage, bamboo craftsmanship, masked dances like Bardochham, and vibrant harvest festivals.

fields.name: Goa
fields.description: Goa is a vibrant coastal tapestry of Konkani traditions, Portuguese colonial architecture, sun-kissed beaches, and a unique composite syncretic ethos known as Sussegad.
fields.cultural_summary: Celebrated for its Azulejos tilecraft, Mando melodies, Fugdi folk dances, and mouthwatering coastal Konkani gastronomy.

fields.name: Meghalaya
fields.description: The Abode of the Clouds, Meghalaya is famous for its mist-shrouded green plateaus, matrilineal Khasi, Garo, and Jaintia societies, and living root bridges.
fields.cultural_summary: Renowned for the 100 Drums Wangala festival, living root architecture, Duitara music, and cane-and-bamboo craftsmanship.

fields.name: Mizoram
fields.description: The Land of the Hill People, Mizoram is characterized by rolling pine hills, close-knit egalitarian villages, and the timeless code of Tlawmngaihna (selfless community service).
fields.cultural_summary: World-famous for the intricate Cheraw bamboo dance, vibrant handwoven Puan textiles, and rhythmic harvest festivals.

fields.name: Nagaland
fields.description: The Land of Festivals, Nagaland is home to 16 recognized major tribes, each with its own language, distinctive warrior tradition, handwoven shawls, and rich oral epics.
fields.cultural_summary: Globally renowned for the Hornbill Festival, ceremonial spear dances, indigenous wood sculpture, and distinctive handloom shawls.

fields.name: Tripura
fields.description: A historic kingdom nestled in riverine hills, Tripura blends indigenous Tipra tribal traditions with royal Manikya architecture and Bengali cultural exchanges.
fields.cultural_summary: Famous for the acrobatic Hojagiri pitcher dance, Kharchi Puja rituals, delicate bamboo screen carving, and Risa handlooms.

fields.name: Jammu & Kashmir
fields.description: The Crown of India, Jammu & Kashmir combines the temple traditions of Jammu, the mystical Sufi gardens and Dal Lake of the Kashmir Valley, and timeless artisanal heritage.
fields.cultural_summary: Famous for Pashmina weaving, Papier-mâché, Santoor music, Rouf dance, and the 36-course royal Wazwan.

fields.name: Ladakh
fields.description: The Land of High Passes, Ladakh is a high-altitude cold desert nestled between the Himalayas and Karakoram, renowned for ancient Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, stupas, and stark sublime landscapes.
fields.cultural_summary: Famous for monastic Cham mask dances, Thangka scroll paintings, butter tea, and the grand Hemis monastic festival.

fields.name: Delhi
fields.description: The historic capital of India, Delhi is an ancient palimpsest of eight historical cities, spanning Indraprastha, the Delhi Sultanate, the Mughal Empire, and modern democratic India.
fields.cultural_summary: Famous for Delhi Gharana classical music, Kathak heritage, Qawwalis of Nizamuddin, Zardozi embroidery, and legendary street food.

fields.name: Chandigarh
fields.description: India’s City Beautiful, Chandigarh is a masterclass in modernist urban architecture designed by Le Corbusier, serving as the joint capital of Punjab and Haryana.
fields.cultural_summary: Known for the whimsical Rock Garden sculptures, Sukhna Lake sunsets, vibrant Bhangra culture, and open garden green spaces.

fields.name: Puducherry
fields.description: A charming coastal union territory known as the French Riviera of the East, blending Tamil heritage with French colonial boulevards, spiritual retreats, and serene coastal tranquility.
fields.cultural_summary: Famous for Garadi folk dance, Franco-Tamil Creole cuisine, Sri Aurobindo Ashram, and handmade terracotta pottery.

fields.name: Andaman and Nicobar
fields.description: An emerald archipelago in the Bay of Bengal, Andaman and Nicobar is an island wonderland of indigenous indigenous tribes, coral reefs, and the sacred national memorial Cellular Jail.
fields.cultural_summary: Known for Nicobarese circle dances, shell and cane crafts, rich maritime folklore, and pristine island ecology.

fields.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
fields.description: A charming coastal and forested union territory in Western India, blending tribal Warli culture with 400 years of Portuguese sea-fortress history in Daman and Diu.
fields.cultural_summary: Famous for Tarpa wind instrument dances, Warli paintings, Diu fortress architecture, and coastal seafood traditions.

fields.name: Lakshadweep
fields.description: A tropical paradise of 36 coral atolls and lagoons in the Arabian Sea, Lakshadweep is celebrated for its serene marine life, coconut groves, and unique Mappila-Malayalam island culture.
fields.cultural_summary: Famous for Kolkali stick dances, Parichakali sword dances, coir matting, and tuna delicacies like Mus Kavaab.

fields.name: Manuscripts & Archives
fields.description: Ancient palm-leaf, birch-bark, copper plate, and illuminated paper codices documenting civilisational knowledge.

fields.name: Oral Literature & Folklore
fields.description: Living oral narratives, bardic ballads, folk epics, lullabies, and communal storytelling traditions.

fields.name: Traditional Knowledge & Science
fields.description: Documented indigenous treatises on Ayurveda, metallurgy, astronomy, architecture (Vastu), and botany.

fields.name: Visual Arts & Painting

fields.name: Clothing, Textiles & Jewellery
fields.description: Handloom weaves, resist-dyeing, tribal metalwork, regional drapery, and festive heirloom ornaments.

fields.name: Baisakhi
fields.description: A major harvest festival celebrating the solar new year and the founding of the Khalsa panth.
fields.cultural_significance: Highly significant for farmers and the Sikh community.

fields.name: Lohri
fields.description: A popular winter folk festival celebrated primarily in the Punjab region.
fields.cultural_significance: Marks the passing of the winter solstice and the arrival of longer days.

fields.name: Maghi
fields.description: The Punjabi festival of Maghi marks the changing of the season and is celebrated with bonfires and feasts.
fields.cultural_significance: Cultural gathering marking warmer days.

fields.name: Pushkar Camel Fair
fields.description: One of the world's largest livestock fairs held on the banks of sacred Lake Pushkar, accompanied by vibrant cultural festivities.
fields.cultural_significance: Unites pilgrims, nomadic pastoralists, and artists in a colourful desert carnival.

fields.name: Gangaur
fields.description: A vibrant festival celebrating Gauri (Goddess Parvati) as the epitome of marital fidelity and spring harvest.
fields.cultural_significance: Women carry decorated clay idols of Isar and Gauri in grand royal processions through heritage streets.

fields.name: Onam
fields.description: A ten-day harvest carnival welcoming the spirit of King Mahabali with floral carpets (Pookkalam) and boat races.
fields.cultural_significance: Kerala's most beloved state festival celebrating harmony, abundance, and unity.

fields.name: Thrissur Pooram
fields.description: The mother of all poorams held at the Vadakkunnathan temple, featuring caparisoned elephants and world-famous Kudamattam umbrella displays.
fields.cultural_significance: Showcases competitive percussion orchestras and magnificent pyrotechnics.

fields.name: Pongal
fields.description: A four-day harvest thanksgiving festival to the Sun God, celebrating the boiling over of newly harvested rice in earthen pots.
fields.cultural_significance: Signifies agricultural abundance, prosperity, and reverence toward cattle and nature.

fields.name: Karthigai Deepam
fields.description: The festival of lights where thousands of clay oil lamps illuminate temples and homes, culminating in the sacred flame on Thiruvannamalai hill.
fields.cultural_significance: Celebrates Lord Shiva manifesting as the infinite column of light.

fields.name: Navratri Garba Festival
fields.description: The world's longest dance festival spanning nine consecutive nights of non-stop community dancing and spiritual devotion.
fields.cultural_significance: Celebrates the victory of Good over Evil with kaleidoscopic attire and live folk orchestras.

fields.name: Uttarayan Kite Festival
fields.description: A grand festival marking the Sun's journey into the Northern Hemisphere, with millions flying vibrant kites across city skies.
fields.cultural_significance: Terraces fill with shouts of "Kai Po Che" amidst festive feasts of Undhiyu and sesame sweets.

fields.name: Ganesh Chaturthi
fields.description: A ten-day mega-festival welcoming Lord Ganesha into homes and giant public pandals with thunderous Dhol-Tasha beats.
fields.cultural_significance: Culminates in grand immersion processions (Visarjan) into the sea amidst chants of "Ganpati Bappa Morya".

fields.name: Gudi Padwa
fields.description: The traditional Maharashtrian New Year celebrated by hoisting a silk-draped Gudi flag outside front doorways.
fields.cultural_significance: Marks the arrival of spring and commemorates the legendary victories of ancient kings.

fields.name: Durga Puja
fields.description: A monumental ten-day festival and UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage honoring Goddess Durga's victory over Mahishasura.
fields.cultural_significance: Transforms Kolkata into the world's largest open-air art installation with hundreds of unique themed pandals.

fields.name: Poila Boishakh
fields.description: The joyous Bengali New Year celebrated with cultural parades, fresh financial ledgers (Haal Khata), and banquets.
fields.cultural_significance: Marked by the customary blessing "Shubho Noboborsho" and family get-togethers.

fields.name: Ratha Yatra of Puri
fields.description: The world-famous Chariot Festival where Lord Jagannath, Balabhadra, and Subhadra are pulled in mammoth wooden chariots.
fields.cultural_significance: Millions of devotees pull the ropes of Nandighosa chariot along the Grand Road (Bada Danda) to Gundicha Temple.

fields.name: Konark Dance Festival
fields.description: An open-air classical dance festival set against the illuminated backdrop of the 13th-century Sun Temple.
fields.cultural_significance: Attracts master dancers of Odissi, Bharatanatyam, and Kathak from across the globe.

fields.name: Rongali Bihu
fields.description: The greatest festival of Assam, heralding the spring agricultural cycle with feasts, folk songs, and community dancing.
fields.cultural_significance: Brings together people of all ethnicities to celebrate renewal and the beginning of the Assamese calendar.

fields.name: Ambubachi Mela
fields.description: An ancient tantric festival celebrated at the Kamakhya Temple atop Nilachal Hill, honoring Mother Earth's fertility.
fields.cultural_significance: Attracts sadhus, ascetics, and pilgrims from across India for sacred ritual blessings.

fields.name: Mysore Dasara
fields.description: A ten-day royal festival where Mysore Palace is illuminated with nearly 100,000 bulbs, ending in the grand Jumboo Savari.
fields.cultural_significance: The golden idol of Goddess Chamundeshwari is paraded atop a decorated elephant in royal splendor.

fields.name: Kambala Buffalo Races
fields.description: An adrenaline-fueled traditional sport where farmers race pairs of buffalos through flooded muddy paddy tracks.
fields.cultural_significance: Celebrates the bond between coastal farmers and their livestock in Dakshina Kannada.

fields.name: Ugadi
fields.description: The Telugu New Year celebrated with the tasting of Ugadi Pachadi, a dish incorporating all six basic tastes.
fields.cultural_significance: Symbolizes that life is an inevitable mixture of happiness, sorrow, surprise, anger, fear, and disgust.

fields.name: Tirupati Brahmotsavam
fields.description: A nine-day mega-festival where Lord Malayappa Swamy is taken out in daily ceremonial processions on divine mounts.
fields.cultural_significance: Attracts hundreds of thousands of pilgrims to the sacred Tirumala hill shrine.

fields.name: Bathukamma Floral Festival
fields.description: A nine-day floral festival celebrated by women who arrange seasonal wildflowers into conical temple towers.
fields.cultural_significance: Women dance in circles singing folk songs celebrating womanhood, nature, and motherly protection.

fields.name: Bonalu
fields.description: A vibrant monsoon festival thanking Goddess Mahakali for communal protection, with women carrying cooked rice pots atop their heads.
fields.cultural_significance: Features colorful Pothuraju dancers whipping the air to ward off negative spirits.

fields.name: Dev Deepawali of Varanasi
fields.description: The celestial night of Kartik Purnima when all eighty-four ghats of Varanasi are illuminated with millions of earthen diyas.
fields.cultural_significance: Celebrates the victory of Lord Shiva over the demon Tripurasura as divine beings descend to bathe in the holy Ganga.

fields.name: Kumbh Mela
fields.description: The world's largest human religious gathering, held every twelve years at the sacred Sangam in Prayagraj.
fields.cultural_significance: Millions of sadhus, pilgrims, and visitors unite to take holy dips in the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and Saraswati.

fields.name: Khajuraho Dance Festival
fields.description: A week-long celebration of classical Indian dance against the illuminated backdrop of 10th-century Chandela temples.
fields.cultural_significance: Masters of all eight classical dance styles perform under open starry skies.

fields.name: Tansen Samaroh Gwalior
fields.description: India's oldest music festival honoring the legendary court musician Mian Tansen near his historic tomb.
fields.cultural_significance: Top classical vocalists and instrumentalists perform round-the-clock raag recitals.

fields.name: Chhath Puja
fields.description: An austere four-day festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya, without priests or idol worship.
fields.cultural_significance: Devotees stand waist-deep in river waters at dawn and dusk offering arghya of seasonal fruits and thekua.

fields.name: Sonepur Cattle Fair
fields.description: One of Asia's largest traditional animal fairs held on the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak rivers on Kartik Purnima.
fields.cultural_significance: Historical trading post for elephants, horses, and livestock alongside vibrant carnival entertainment.

fields.name: Sarhul Spring Festival
fields.description: The greatest festival of the Oraon, Munda, and Santhal tribes, worshipping the blooming Sal trees.
fields.cultural_significance: Villagers take sacred Sal blossoms to their homes, celebrating the spiritual wedding of the Sun and Mother Earth.

fields.name: Karma Festival
fields.description: A sacred tribal festival where young boys and girls plant Karma tree branches in the village akhara to pray for prosperity.
fields.cultural_significance: Accompanied by all-night dancing, storytelling, and community bonding.

fields.name: Bastar Dussehra
fields.description: A unique 75-day festival celebrated by tribal communities without burning effigies of Ravana, honoring Goddess Danteshwari.
fields.cultural_significance: Features the ceremonial construction and pulling of a massive double-decker wooden chariot by hundreds of tribal devotees.

fields.name: Madai Fair
fields.description: A vibrant nomadic tribal fair held across Bastar villages where local village gods are brought together in grand processions.
fields.cultural_significance: Accompanied by traditional folk sports, cock fights, and festive open-air bazaars.

fields.name: Kullu Dussehra
fields.description: A week-long international festival where over two hundred village deities (Devtas) assemble in Dhalpur ground to pay homage to Lord Raghunath.
fields.cultural_significance: Unlike other Dussehra celebrations, it begins on the day when celebrations end elsewhere in India.

fields.name: Minjar Fair of Chamba
fields.description: A historic monsoon harvest carnival commemorating the blooming of maize shoots (Minjar), marked by processions to the Ravi River.
fields.cultural_significance: People pin golden silk tassels to their garments symbolizing communal harmony and agricultural gratitude.

fields.name: Nanda Devi Raj Jat
fields.description: A challenging three-week 280-kilometer barefoot pilgrimage following a four-horned ram to high-altitude Roopkund and Homkund.
fields.cultural_significance: One of the world's most awe-inspiring mountain pilgrimages honoring Goddess Nanda's return to Mount Kailash.

fields.name: Phool Dei Spring Festival
fields.description: A delightful spring festival where young children go from doorstep to doorstep sprinkling wild yellow and white mountain blossoms.
fields.cultural_significance: Children sing wishing households prosperity and health, receiving sweet rice snacks (Papdi) in return.

fields.name: Surajkund International Crafts Mela
fields.description: The world's largest international crafts fair set around the 10th-century sun pool in Faridabad.
fields.cultural_significance: Brings together master craftspersons, folk dancers, and culinary artists from dozens of countries and every Indian state.

fields.name: Pinjore Heritage Festival
fields.description: A celebration of Mughal garden heritage, classical performing arts, and traditional crafts in the historic Yadavindra Gardens.
fields.cultural_significance: Illuminates tiered fountains and historic pavilions with music recitals.

fields.name: Yaoshang
fields.description: The five-day festival of colors celebrated with Thabal Chongba (moonlit circle dance), youth sports competitions, and prayer.
fields.cultural_significance: Transforms the entire state into a joyful arena of youthful camaraderie and athletic contests.

fields.name: Sangai Festival
fields.description: Manipur's premier tourism festival named after the rare brow-antlered dancing deer found exclusively in Keibul Lamjao National Park.
fields.cultural_significance: Showcases indigenous polo matches, boat races, handlooms, and cultural performances.

fields.name: Pang Lhabsol
fields.description: A unique festival commemorating the historic blood brotherhood signed between Lepcha and Bhutia chieftains witnessed by Mount Kanchenjunga.
fields.cultural_significance: Features sacred warrior dances and blessings for the ecological balance of the Himalayas.

fields.name: Losar (Tibetan New Year)
fields.description: The joyous Tibetan New Year celebrated with monastery cham dances, preparation of Gutuk dumplings, and family feasts.
fields.cultural_significance: Welcomes new beginnings, cleansing evil spirits from the previous year.

fields.name: Losar & Nyokum
fields.description: Losar marks the Tibetan and Monpa New Year with monastic dances, while Nyokum is the grand agricultural festival of the Nyishi tribe.
fields.cultural_significance: Unites communities in prayers for bumper harvests, peace, and protection against natural calamities.

fields.name: Shigmo & Feast of St. Francis Xavier
fields.description: Shigmo is Goa’s vibrant spring carnival celebrated with street floats and temple lamps, while the Feast of St. Francis Xavier draws millions to Old Goa.
fields.cultural_significance: Illustrates Goa’s unique multi-faith harmony and shared festive celebrations.

fields.name: Wangala (100 Drums Festival)
fields.description: The post-harvest thanksgiving festival of the Garo tribe, featuring 100 drummers playing simultaneously in unison.
fields.cultural_significance: Offers thanksgiving to Misi Saljong, the Sun-god of fertility, uniting hundreds of Garo villages in rhythm.

fields.name: Chapchar Kut
fields.description: The grand spring harvest festival celebrated after the clearing of jhum forest slopes, marked by community singing and mass Cheraw dancing.
fields.cultural_significance: The ultimate expression of Mizo joy, reconciliation, and community egalitarian bonding.

fields.name: Hornbill Festival & Moatsu
fields.description: The Festival of Festivals held at Kisama Heritage Village, showcasing the dances, crafts, music, and food of all 16 Naga tribes.
fields.cultural_significance: Serves as an extraordinary platform for inter-tribal cultural harmony and global heritage tourism.

fields.name: Kharchi Puja (Festival of 14 Gods)
fields.description: A week-long royal temple festival in Old Agartala honoring the Fourteen Deities, purifying the Mother Earth after her fertility period.
fields.cultural_significance: Unites both tribal and non-tribal communities in shared ancient sacrificial and temple rituals.

fields.name: Herath (Shivratri) & Tulip Festival
fields.description: Herath is the Kashmiri Pandit celebration of Shiva and Parvati with earthen pitcher rituals (Vatuk), while the Tulip Festival marks bloom along Dal Lake.
fields.cultural_significance: Celebrates the distinct rituals and seasonal beauty of the valley with shared confectionery and walnuts.

fields.name: Hemis Festival & Losar
fields.description: Hemis commemorates the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava with vibrant mask dances, while Losar marks the Ladakhi New Year.
fields.cultural_significance: Draws thousands of pilgrims and global travelers into the sacred courtyards of the historic Drukpa monastery.

fields.name: Qutub Festival & Phool Walon Ki Sair
fields.description: Phool Walon Ki Sair is a historic syncretic festival where floral fans are offered both at the shrine of Qutbuddin Bakhtiar Kaki and the Yogmaya Temple.
fields.cultural_significance: A historic 19th-century symbol of Delhi’s secular composite culture (Ganga-Jamuni Tehzeeb).

fields.name: Chandigarh Rose Festival & Mango Mela
fields.description: A massive three-day floral extravaganza held at the Zakir Hussain Rose Garden, showcasing hundreds of rare rose species, folk dances, and cultural contests.
fields.cultural_significance: Celebrates nature, civic pride, and seasonal blooms in India’s planned city.

fields.name: Fête de Puducherry & Masi Magam
fields.description: Fête de Puducherry celebrates national de jure transfer day with carnivals, while Masi Magam features hundreds of temple deities taking a ceremonial holy sea bath.
fields.cultural_significance: A vibrant convergence of sacred coastal temple rituals and French-Indian civic festivals.

fields.name: Island Tourism Festival & Subhash Mela
fields.description: A grand 10-day cultural showcase at Port Blair celebrating mainland and indigenous island heritage, arts, and music.
fields.cultural_significance: Unites diverse communities across the archipelago into a joyful celebration of national unity.

fields.name: Tarpa Festival & Nariyal Poornima
fields.description: Celebrates the beginning of the fishing season with coconuts offered to the Arabian Sea, alongside tribal dances and craft fairs.
fields.cultural_significance: Brings together tribal villagers and coastal fishing communities in shared thanksgiving.

fields.name: Eid-ul-Fitr & Milad-un-Nabi
fields.description: Celebrated with widespread prayer gatherings at historical coral-stone mosques (Ujra Mosque), community feasts, and Kolkali performances.
fields.cultural_significance: Unites families across all coral atolls in feasting, reconciliation, and vibrant cultural performances.

fields.name: Makki di Roti & Sarson da Saag
fields.description: A traditional winter dish made of corn flour bread and mustard greens.
fields.ingredients: Corn flour, mustard greens, spices, butter.
fields.cultural_context: The quintessential winter comfort food of rural Punjab.

fields.name: Amritsari Kulcha
fields.description: A crisp, flaky bread stuffed with spiced potatoes and baked in a tandoor.
fields.ingredients: Flour, potatoes, spices, butter.
fields.cultural_context: A famous street food from Amritsar.

fields.name: Punjabi Lassi
fields.description: A rich, creamy, yogurt-based drink served in tall brass glasses.
fields.ingredients: Yogurt, sugar, cream.
fields.cultural_context: A refreshing staple drink accompanying heavy Punjabi meals.

fields.name: Dal Baati Churma
fields.description: A trio comprising hard wheat dough balls baked on cow-dung fire or tandoor, spicy mixed lentil stew, and sweetened crushed wheat crumble.
fields.ingredients: Wheat flour, mixed lentils, ghee, jaggery, cumin, garlic, cloves.
fields.cultural_context: The quintessential Rajasthani meal born from warrior campaigns in desert conditions.

fields.name: Ker Sangri
fields.description: A tart, savory stir-fry of wild desert berries (Ker) and dried desert beans (Sangri) seasoned with red chilies and mustard oil.
fields.ingredients: Ker berries, Sangri beans, dry red chilies, turmeric, amchur (mango powder), mustard oil.
fields.cultural_context: A prized famine-survival delicacy celebrated as royal banqueting fare.

fields.name: Appam with Ishtu
fields.description: Lacy, fermented rice and coconut milk pancakes with a fluffy center, paired with a mild, aromatic vegetable or meat coconut stew.
fields.ingredients: Fermented rice batter, coconut milk, curry leaves, ginger, green chilies, shallots.
fields.cultural_context: A beloved Christian Syrian and Kerala household breakfast staple.

fields.name: Kerala Sadya
fields.description: A grand vegetarian feast of over twenty-four traditional dishes served ceremoniously on a fresh plantain leaf.
fields.ingredients: Red Matta rice, Sambar, Avial, Thoran, Payasam, Olan, Injipuli, Pachadi.
fields.cultural_context: The ultimate cultural banquet celebrating Onam, festivals, and weddings.

fields.name: Masala Dosa with Sambar
fields.description: A paper-thin, crispy fermented rice and lentil crepe stuffed with spiced potato masala, served with piping hot lentil stew and coconut chutney.
fields.ingredients: Parboiled rice, urad dal, potatoes, mustard seeds, curry leaves, tamarind, sambar spices.
fields.cultural_context: The beloved South Indian staple enjoyed worldwide.

fields.name: Chettinad Curry
fields.description: A fiery, deeply aromatic curry enriched with freshly roasted spices including kalpasi (black stone flower) and star anise.
fields.ingredients: Chicken or vegetables, shallots, fennel, black peppercorns, star anise, poppy seeds, curry leaves.
fields.cultural_context: Crafted by the aristocratic Chettiar merchant community of Tamil Nadu.

fields.name: Gujarati Thali
fields.description: A balanced, wholesome platter incorporating sweet, salty, spicy, and tangy notes across bread, lentils, vegetables, and snacks.
fields.ingredients: Kadhi, Gujarati Dal, Shaak, Rotli, Puri, Farsan, Chutney, Shrikhand, Rice.
fields.cultural_context: Emphasizes Ayurvedic nutritional harmony with distinctive gentle sweetness.

fields.name: Khaman Dhokla
fields.description: A spongy, steamed snack made from fermented gram flour, tempered with mustard seeds, sesame, curry leaves, and green chilies.
fields.ingredients: Gram flour (Besan), eno or fruit salt, lemon juice, mustard seeds, green chilies, cilantro.
fields.cultural_context: The quintessential Gujarati street food and tea-time delicacy.

fields.name: Puran Poli
fields.description: A delicate, sweet flatbread stuffed with a fragrant filling of boiled chana dal, jaggery, cardamom, and nutmeg, slathered in pure ghee.
fields.ingredients: Chana dal, jaggery, wheat flour, cardamom, nutmeg, ghee.
fields.cultural_context: The sacred festival dessert cooked on Holi, Gudi Padwa, and Ganesh Chaturthi.

fields.name: Misal Pav
fields.description: A fiery sprouted-moth bean curry topped with crunchy farsan, onions, coriander, and lime, soaked up with buttered pav bread.
fields.ingredients: Sprouted moth beans (matki), onions, coconut, goda masala, farsan, pav bread.
fields.cultural_context: Maharashtra's legendary breakfast and street-food classic, known for its spicy "kat" gravy.

fields.name: Machher Jhol with Rice
fields.description: A light, fragrant mustard or cumin-infused fish curry prepared with fresh freshwater carp (Rohu or Katla) and tender vegetables.
fields.ingredients: Freshwater fish, mustard oil, paanch phoron, potatoes, ginger, green chilies.
fields.cultural_context: The daily culinary soul of every Bengali home.

fields.name: Kosha Mangsho & Mishti Doi
fields.description: Slow-cooked, velvety spicy mutton curry paired with thick, caramelised sweet yogurt baked in earthen pots.
fields.ingredients: Mutton, mustard oil, onions, whole spices, curd, sweetened condensed milk.
fields.cultural_context: The crown jewel of Bengali Sunday feasts and festive celebrations.

fields.name: Dalma
fields.description: A wholesome, nutritious lentil dish simmered with raw papaya, plantain, pumpkin, and tempered with roasted cumin and ghee.
fields.ingredients: Toor dal, raw vegetables, ginger, pancha phutana, ghee, roasted cumin-chili powder.
fields.cultural_context: A revered temple offering in Puri Jagannath's Mahaprasad.

fields.name: Chhena Poda
fields.description: The quintessential baked cottage cheese dessert, caramelized for hours until a golden-brown crust envelops its tender center.
fields.ingredients: Fresh cottage cheese (chhena), sugar, cardamom, cashews, raisins, ghee.
fields.cultural_context: Invented in Nayagarh, Chhena Poda is celebrated as India's original baked cheesecake.

fields.name: Khaar
fields.description: An alkaline signature starter prepared by filtering water through sun-dried, burned banana peel ashes with raw papaya.
fields.ingredients: Filtered banana ash water (Khaar), raw papaya, mustard seeds, garlic, fish head or pulses.
fields.cultural_context: Assam's unique cleansing palate cleanser believed to improve digestion.

fields.name: Masor Tenga
fields.description: A light, refreshing sour fish curry infused with elephant apple (Ou Tenga), tomatoes, or lemon juice.
fields.ingredients: Freshwater fish, elephant apple or lemon, mustard oil, green chilies, fenugreek.
fields.cultural_context: The soul-soothing summer meal of rural Assam paired with steaming Joha rice.

fields.name: Bisi Bele Bath
fields.description: A comforting, spicy one-pot dish of rice, lentils, assorted vegetables, and a proprietary aromatic spice mix fried in ghee.
fields.ingredients: Rice, toor dal, vegetables, bisi bele bath powder, tamarind, cashews, pure ghee.
fields.cultural_context: A timeless culinary jewel created in the royal kitchens of the Mysore Palace.

fields.name: Mysore Pak
fields.description: A decadent sweet made of roasted gram flour, generous pure ghee, and sugar, famous for its melt-in-mouth texture.
fields.ingredients: Gram flour (besan), pure desi ghee, sugar syrup, cardamom.
fields.cultural_context: Created in 1935 by palace royal chef Kakasura Madappa for the Maharaja of Mysore.

fields.name: Pesarattu with Allam Pachadi
fields.description: A crisp, wholesome crepe made from soaked whole green gram (moong dal), paired with spicy-sweet ginger chutney.
fields.ingredients: Whole green moong dal, ginger, cumin, green chilies, onions, tamarind jaggery chutney.
fields.cultural_context: Andhra Pradesh's signature high-protein breakfast delight.

fields.name: Gongura Pachadi
fields.description: A spicy, tangy pickle prepared from red sorrel leaves, roasted dry red chilies, garlic, and cold-pressed sesame oil.
fields.ingredients: Gongura (sorrel) leaves, red chilies, garlic, mustard seeds, fenugreek, oil.
fields.cultural_context: Known as the "Andhra Shakahaara King", an indispensable accompaniment to hot steamed rice.

fields.name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
fields.description: Fragrant basmati rice and marinated meat slow-cooked in a sealed clay handi over charcoal with saffron and mint.
fields.ingredients: Basmati rice, chicken/mutton, yogurt, fried onions (birista), saffron, cardamom, cloves, mint.
fields.cultural_context: The world-famous jewel of Nizami cuisine perfected over centuries in Hyderabad.

fields.name: Sarva Pindi
fields.description: A savory, crispy circular pancake made from rice flour, roasted peanuts, chana dal, sesame seeds, and curry leaves.
fields.ingredients: Rice flour, roasted peanuts, chana dal, white sesame seeds, green chilies, onions.
fields.cultural_context: A wholesome traditional afternoon snack from rural Telangana.

fields.name: Awadhi Dum Biryani & Galouti Kebab
fields.description: Melt-in-the-mouth smoked kebabs flavored with over 150 royal spices, paired with fragrant layered dum biryani.
fields.ingredients: Minced meat, raw papaya, potli masala, saffron, basmati rice, rose water, kewra.
fields.cultural_context: Created for the toothless Nawab Asad-ud-Daula by master royal bawarchis of Lucknow.

fields.name: Banarasi Paan & Malaiyyo
fields.description: Winter milk foam infused with saffron and pistachios, followed by the iconic sweet betel leaf prepared with fragrant gulkand.
fields.ingredients: Milk froth, saffron, pistachios, betel leaf, gulkand, supari, silver vark.
fields.cultural_context: The legendary sweet finish to a royal dining experience in Kashi.

fields.name: Poha Jalebi
fields.description: Flattened rice tossed with mustard seeds, curry leaves, onions, and crunchy sev, served alongside piping-hot golden jalebis.
fields.ingredients: Poha (flattened rice), onions, fennel seeds, sev, green chilies, jalebi.
fields.cultural_context: The unbeatable breakfast icon across streets in Indore, Bhopal, and Ujjain.

fields.name: Dal Bafla
fields.description: Soft, boiled-and-baked wheat dough balls bathed in pure ghee, served with spicy toor dal and coriander-mint chutney.
fields.ingredients: Wheat flour, semolina, toor dal, ghee, cumin, coriander, spices.
fields.cultural_context: Malwa's beloved cousin of the Rajasthani baati, loved for its softer, pillowy texture.

fields.name: Litti Chokha
fields.description: Roasted whole-wheat dough balls stuffed with spiced roasted gram flour (sattu), served with smoky roasted eggplant-tomato mash.
fields.ingredients: Wheat flour, sattu (gram flour), ajwain, kalonji, mustard oil, brinjal, tomatoes, garlic, ghee.
fields.cultural_context: The nutritious, smoky soul food of Bihar celebrated across the nation.

fields.name: Thekua & Khaja
fields.description: Crispy deep-fried sweet biscuits flavored with fennel and cardamom, and flaky layered pastries from Silao soaked in syrup.
fields.ingredients: Wheat flour, jaggery or sugar, ghee, fennel seeds, cardamom, refined flour.
fields.cultural_context: The revered prasad of Chhath Puja and a cherished festive souvenir from Nalanda.

fields.name: Dhuska with Ghugni
fields.description: A savory deep-fried pancake made from soaked rice and chana dal batter, served with spicy black chickpea curry.
fields.ingredients: Rice, chana dal, urad dal, green chilies, ginger, black chickpeas, spices.
fields.cultural_context: Jharkhand's favorite breakfast street food, loved for its crispy exterior and soft center.

fields.name: Rugda Curry
fields.description: A seasonal wild mushroom found under Sal forest canopies during monsoons, cooked in a rich, mustard-onion gravy.
fields.ingredients: Fresh rugda mushrooms, onions, ginger-garlic paste, mustard oil, garam masala.
fields.cultural_context: A prized natural delicacy that boasts a meaty texture and deep umami flavor.

fields.name: Faraa & Chila
fields.description: Steamed rice dumplings seasoned with mustard seeds and curry leaves, paired with crisp savory rice pancakes and tangy tomato chutney.
fields.ingredients: Rice flour, chana dal stuffing, green chilies, mustard seeds, curry leaves.
fields.cultural_context: Healthy, comforting staples consumed daily in rural Chhattisgarhi homes.

fields.name: Muthia & Bafauri
fields.description: Steamed spiced gram dumplings lightly pan-fried in oil, and crunchy vegetable patties prepared without deep-frying.
fields.ingredients: Chana dal, leafy greens, onions, ginger-garlic paste, sesame seeds.
fields.cultural_context: Nutritious traditional snacks that demonstrate clever indigenous oil-free cooking techniques.

fields.name: Himachali Dham
fields.description: A ceremonial multi-course vegetarian banquet cooked exclusively by traditional Brahman chefs called Botis in brass pots.
fields.ingredients: Basmati rice, Madra (kidney beans in yogurt), Chana Khatta, Mah ki Dal, Meetha Bhat.
fields.cultural_context: Served without onions or garlic on dried leaf plates at festive celebrations.

fields.name: Siddu with Pure Ghee
fields.description: A steamed oval wheat bread stuffed with a savory filling of crushed walnuts, poppy seeds, and spices, drenched in melting desi ghee.
fields.ingredients: Wheat flour, yeast, walnuts, poppy seeds, green chilies, coriander, pure ghee.
fields.cultural_context: The ultimate winter comfort food of Himachal that keeps mountain dwellers warm in snowy months.

fields.name: Kafuli & Chainsoo
fields.description: A velvety green puree of wild mountain greens (spinach and fenugreek) and a roasted black gram curry cooked in an iron kadhai.
fields.ingredients: Spinach, methi, rice paste, black gram, garlic, jakhiya seeds, mustard oil.
fields.cultural_context: Rich in minerals, iron, and warmth, the signature daily nourishment of Garhwal.

fields.name: Bal Mithai of Almora
fields.description: A brown, fudge-like sweet made by roasting evaporated milk (khoya) for hours until caramelized, coated in tiny sugar pearls.
fields.ingredients: Khoya (milk solids), sugar, cardamom, white sugar balls.
fields.cultural_context: The beloved hundred-year-old confectionery pride of Kumaon.

fields.name: Bajra Khichdi with Ghee & Chhachh
fields.description: A hearty winter porridge of coarse pearl millet and moong dal, served with generous dollops of homemade white butter and cold buttermilk.
fields.ingredients: Pearl millet (bajra), moong dal, desi ghee, cumin, green chilies, chaas.
fields.cultural_context: The rustic powerhouse meal that fuels Haryana's agriculturalists and champion wrestlers.

fields.name: Kadhi Pakora & Kachri ki Chutney
fields.description: A tart, creamy yogurt-gram flour curry studded with crisp fritters, paired with wild desert cucumber chutney.
fields.ingredients: Sour curd, besan, fenugreek seeds, mustard seeds, kachri (wild melon), garlic, red chilies.
fields.cultural_context: The quintessential comforting home meal of rural Haryana.

fields.name: Kangshoi
fields.description: A healthy, oil-free vegetable stew simmered with seasonal green vegetables, ginger, onions, and sun-dried or fermented fish.
fields.ingredients: Seasonal greens, fermented fish (Ngari), ginger, green chilies, cilantro.
fields.cultural_context: The nourishing comfort soup eaten daily in every Manipuri household.

fields.name: Singju Salad & Eromba
fields.description: A fiery, fresh salad of finely shredded vegetables tossed with roasted chickpea flour, perilla seeds, and fermented fish paste.
fields.ingredients: Cabbage, lotus stems, perilla seeds (Thoiding), red chilies, fermented fish, herbs.
fields.cultural_context: Bursting with complex textures and intense aromatic flavors.

fields.name: Steamed Momos with Gundruk Soup
fields.description: Delicate steamed dumplings stuffed with organic minced vegetables or meat, served with fermented leafy green soup.
fields.ingredients: Flour, cabbage, onions, garlic, ginger, fermented mustard greens (gundruk), tomato sesame chili dip.
fields.cultural_context: The universally beloved mountain staple perfected in the street kitchens of Gangtok.

fields.name: Thukpa & Phagshapa
fields.description: A warming noodle soup packed with seasonal greens and spices, accompanied by strips of pork or tofu cooked with radishes and dried chilies.
fields.ingredients: Handmade egg or wheat noodles, clear broth, bok choy, radishes, dried red chilies, ginger.
fields.cultural_context: Wholesome organic comfort food designed to counter cold Himalayan winds.

fields.name: Thukpa & Zan with Bamboo Shoot
fields.description: Hearty Himalayan noodle soup combined with Zan (millet porridge) flavored with wild fermented bamboo shoot and smoked meat.
fields.ingredients: Handmade wheat noodles, mountain herbs, fermented bamboo shoot (Ekung), roasted millet, wild ginger, broth.
fields.cultural_context: Nutritious mountain cuisine designed to sustain energy in high-altitude sub-zero climates.

fields.name: Goan Fish Curry & Bebinca
fields.description: Tangy coconut and kokum-infused kingfish curry paired with steamed red rice, finished with multi-layered baked Bebinca dessert.
fields.ingredients: Fresh kingfish, freshly grated coconut, Kashmiri chilies, kokum, coriander seeds, coconut milk, jaggery, eggs, ghee.
fields.cultural_context: The quintessential Goan midday meal, balancing Portuguese baking techniques with ancient Saraswat coastal spices.

fields.name: Jadoh & Dohneiiong with Tungrymbai
fields.description: Fragrant Khasi red rice cooked with delicate meat broth, paired with pork cooked in roasted black sesame paste.
fields.ingredients: Short-grain red rice, ginger, onions, wild black sesame paste (Neiiong), fermented soy beans (Tungrymbai), bay leaves.
fields.cultural_context: The cornerstone of Khasi festive meals, rich in savory, nutty flavors developed from indigenous fermentation.

fields.name: Bai & Sawhchiar
fields.description: Subtle vegetable and pork stew cooked without oil, seasoned with fermented pork fat, wild local herbs, and local soda (Ching).
fields.ingredients: Mustard leaves, tender bamboo shoots, local beans, Ching (filtered wood ash water), pork fat, red rice.
fields.cultural_context: Organic, wholesome, and oil-free cuisine highlighting the pure natural flavors of high-altitude forest produce.

fields.name: Smoked Pork with Axone & Raja Mircha
fields.description: Tender wood-smoked pork slow-cooked with fermented soya bean cakes (Axone) and fiery Naga King Chili (Ghost Pepper).
fields.ingredients: Hearth-smoked pork, Axone (fermented soybean paste), Raja Mircha (Bhut Jolokia), local ginger, bamboo shoots.
fields.cultural_context: The definitive celebratory dish of Nagaland, celebrated for its complex earthy aroma and intense natural heat.

fields.name: Mui Borok & Chakhwi with Berma
fields.description: Traditional Tipra cuisine cooked without oil using Berma (fermented fish paste), green vegetables, and alkaline bamboo ash.
fields.ingredients: Berma (sun-dried fermented fish), bamboo shoots, green chilies, wild beans, local herbs, rice flour.
fields.cultural_context: Nutritious, gut-friendly indigenous food that sustains community health through traditional fermentation.

fields.name: Kashmiri Wazwan & Kahwa
fields.description: A royal 36-course banquet featuring Rogan Josh, Rista, and Gustaba simmered in yogurt and saffron, finished with cardamom Kahwa green tea.
fields.ingredients: Mutton, Kashmiri cockscomb herb (Mawal), dried fennel powder, ginger powder, saffron, green cardamom, cinnamon, almonds.
fields.cultural_context: Prepared by master chefs (Vastas) for weddings and state banquets, served in giant shared copper platters (Trami).

fields.name: Skyu & Gur Gur Butter Tea
fields.description: Traditional thumb-pressed wheat pasta stew simmered with root vegetables, served alongside salty, warm yak-butter tea.
fields.ingredients: Whole wheat dough, root turnips, wild mountain peas, mutton or dried vegetables, brick tea, yak butter, rock salt.
fields.cultural_context: Vital cold-climate nourishment providing sustained thermoregulation and hydration in arid 12,000-foot altitudes.

fields.name: Dilli Mughlai Nihari & Chaat
fields.description: Slow-cooked overnight beef/shank Nihari stew simmered with 50 spices, alongside iconic Chandni Chowk street Chaat and stuffed Parathas.
fields.ingredients: Meat shanks, bone marrow, brown onions, mace, nutmeg, star anise, rose water, yoghurt, tamarind, cumin, crispy papdi.
fields.cultural_context: The legendary gastronomic legacy of Shahjahanabad, combining royal imperial kitchens with bustling bazaar street flavors.

fields.name: Chole Bhature & Malai Lassi
fields.description: Spicy dark chickpeas stewed in roasted tea water and anardana, served with puffed golden Bhature and thick sweet curd lassi.
fields.ingredients: Kabuli chickpeas, pomegranate seeds (anardana), black tea bags, carom seeds, refined flour, curd, cardamom, malai.
fields.cultural_context: The quintessential North Indian indulgence, synonymous with lively family morning breakfasts across the city.

fields.name: Franco-Tamil Creole Cuisine
fields.description: Unique culinary blend featuring Bouillabaisse-inspired Meen Curry, Vindaloo with French wine vinegar, and baguette pairings.
fields.ingredients: Fresh ocean seafood, coconut milk, curry leaves, tamarind, Dijon-style mustard, mild spices, fresh baguettes.
fields.cultural_context: A distinct historic cuisine developed by French-Indian household chefs, balancing European subtlety with South Indian spice.

fields.name: Andaman Coconut Seafood Curry
fields.description: Succulent fresh reef fish and prawns simmered in freshly squeezed coconut milk with curry leaves and crushed island black pepper.
fields.ingredients: Fresh coastal prawns, red snapper, coconut milk, mustard seeds, curry leaves, ginger, black pepper, lime juice.
fields.cultural_context: Fresh tropical coastal cuisine celebrating the pristine marine bounty of the Bay of Bengal.

fields.name: Ubadiyu & Damania Fish Curry
fields.description: Fragrant winter vegetables slow-cooked in earthen pots buried upside-down in smoking farm embers, paired with Portuguese-Konkani fish curry.
fields.ingredients: Wild yam, broad beans (papdi), potatoes, wild carom herbs, fresh pomfret, kokum, coconut paste, green chilies.
fields.cultural_context: Earthy, smoky village feast prepared collectively after the winter harvest in open farmlands.

fields.name: Mus Kavaab & Batla Appam
fields.description: Spicy, tender boneless Skipjack tuna skewers marinated in coconut and ground island spices, paired with soft steamed rice appams.
fields.ingredients: Fresh Skipjack tuna (Mus), ground coconut, shallots, garlic, dried red chilies, turmeric, curry leaves, rice batter.
fields.cultural_context: The signature delicacy of the atolls, built around the sustainable pole-and-line tuna fishing tradition.

fields.description: The sacred single-string Pena bowed lute accompanies ancient Thang-Ta combat chants during Meitei Lai Haraoba rituals.
Pung Cholom drum rhythms set the explosive tempo and martial footwork for Thang-Ta sword routines.
The legendary embroidered Shaphee Lanphee shawl was historically awarded by Meitei royalty as a medal of honor to champion Thang-Ta warriors.
The national epic of Khamba and Thoibi features heroic combat duels honoring traditional Thang-Ta martial courage.
Shares sacred martial weapon arts origins with Jharkhand's Paika sword-and-shield warrior dance.
Parallels Uttarakhand's Choliya martial sword dance in using weaponry to ward off malevolent spirits.
The deep syncopated heartbeat of the double-headed Dhol drum drives every Bhangra step and leap.
The high-pitched single-string plucks of the Tumbi define the iconic modern and traditional Bhangra melodies.
Bhangra (traditionally danced by men) and Giddha (danced by women) form the twin harvest celebratory pillars of Punjab.
Giddha dancers wear colorful dupattas richly embroidered with generational geometric Phulkari needlework.
Both Bhangra and Gujarat’s Garba celebrate seasonal harvest and community unity through rhythmic circle choreography.
While Ghoomar embodies royal courtly etiquette, Kalbelia expresses nomadic desert serpent rhythms across Rajasthan.
The ancient bowed Ravanahatha provides the haunting modal melodies accompanying Rajasthani folk songs.
Wandering Bhopa bards recite the tragic romance of Dhola and Maru accompanied by the bowing of the Ravanahatha.
The thunderous Chenda drum builds the dramatic crescendos accompanying demonic clashes in Kathakali.
Theyyam's towering painted headgear and spirit channelings served as archaic ritual ancestors to Kathakali theater.
The sacred vibrations of the Nadaswaram reed horn herald temple ceremonies where Bharatanatyam was historically offered.
The Saraswati Veena provides the nuanced gamaka microtones that guide Bharatanatyam abhinaya facial expressions.
Bharatanatyam dancers wear pure Kanchipuram silk pleats woven with temple tower (gopuram) motifs that fan out during araimandi bends.
Both Bharatanatyam and Odisha's Odissi descend from ancient Natya Shastra temple dancer (Devadasi/Mahari) lineages.
Garba circle clapping leads directly into high-energy Dandiya Raas stick percussion during the nine nights of Navratri.
Patola double-ikat sarees with royal elephant and parrot motifs are prized as the most auspicious heirloom garments worn at Garba celebrations.
Warli murals share deep philosophical and visual kinship with Jharkhand's Sohrai ritual wall paintings.
Lavani folk dance rhythms and Powada warrior ballads evolved side-by-side in 17th-century Maratha military encampments.
Lavani dancers drape opulent nine-yard Paithani silk sarees with peacock pallus to execute acrobatic spins and gestures.
Kathak dancers under Awadh court patronage wore layered Banarasi silk angrakhas that swirl during rapid chakkars (spins).
Kathak footwork is accompanied by the evocative Banaras Thumri melodies played on the sacred Shehnai of Varanasi.

fields.title: Silappadikaram (The Tale of an Anklet)
fields.brief_intro: One of the Five Great Epics of Tamil literature, narrating the virtuous Kannagi’s moral trial, Kovalan’s tragic fate, and the burning of Madurai against royal injustice.
fields.synopsis: Silappadikaram is an unparalleled jewel of early Indian literature. It follows Kovalan, a merchant of Poompuhar, his noble wife Kannagi, and Madhavi, an accomplished court dancer. After losing his fortune, Kovalan journeys with Kannagi to Madurai to rebuild their life by selling her ruby-filled anklet. Wrongfully accused of stealing the Queen’s pearl anklet by a dishonest court goldsmith, Kovalan is executed without fair trial by the Pandyan king Nedunjeliyan. Kannagi shatters the remaining anklet in the royal court, exposing the king’s catastrophic error, causing the king and queen to die of shock. Kannagi invokes Agni and burns corrupt Madurai, becoming celebrated as Pattini Devi (the embodiment of righteousness).
fields.cultural_significance: Silappadikaram bridges social reality, fine arts, urban planning, dance musicology (Arangetru Kadai), and justice. It establishes the Pattini cult revered across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Sri Lanka. Unlike courtly panegyrics, its protagonist is an ordinary merchant woman whose virtue subverts absolute monarchical authority.
fields.historical_context: Composed during the late Sangam or post-Sangam era, the text provides vivid descriptions of major ports like Kaveripoompattinam (Poompuhar), music theory (Yazh tuning), and inter-kingdom diplomatic relationships between Cheras, Cholas, and Pandyas.
fields.themes: Dharma (Aram), royal accountability, unyielding justice, maritime trade, Bharatanatyam precursors, and feminine spiritual authority.
fields.available_translations: Translated into English by Alain Daniélou (1965), R. Parthasarathy (Columbia University Press, 1993, Sahitya Akademi Award winner), and multiple modern Indian languages.
fields.custodian_collection: U. V. Swaminatha Iyer Library, Chennai; palm-leaf recensions recovered from Thanjavur and Tirunelveli.
fields.rights_attribution: Ancient Classical Heritage (Public Domain); modern critical texts preserved by Sahitya Akademi.
fields.excerpt_content:
"Oh witness of the Sun! Is it righteous that my innocent husband be struck down as a thief?
If I be chaste and truthful, let the city of Madurai know the blazing fire of injustice!"
With trembling hands, Kannagi broke her gold anklet upon the throne steps;
Rubies spilled across the polished marble, while the royal queen's anklet bore only pearls.
The Pandyan King gasped: "I am no king, I am the robber. Today the justice of the Pandyas is extinguished."

fields.title: Guru Granth Sahib (Adi Granth)
fields.author_creator: Compiled by Guru Arjan Dev (1604 CE), conferred eternal Guruship by Guru Gobind Singh (1708 CE)
fields.language: Sant Bhasha (Punjabi, Braj Bhasha, Persian, Sanskrit, Awadhi, Marathi dialectic blend)
fields.brief_intro: The eternal living Guru of Sikhism, comprising 1,430 Angs (pages) of profound philosophical poetry arranged across 31 classical musical Ragas.
fields.synopsis: The Guru Granth Sahib is unique among world scriptures for its radically universalist and interfaith composition. Along with the divine revelations of six Sikh Gurus (Guru Nanak, Guru Angad, Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das, Guru Arjan, and Guru Tegh Bahadur), it lovingly canonizes the sacred compositions (Bani) of 15 non-Sikh Bhagats and Sufi saints across India—including Bhagat Kabir, Bhagat Namdev (Maharashtra), Bhagat Ravidas, Bhagat Jaidev (Bengal), Bhagat Ramanand, and Sheikh Farid (Punjab Sufi). Set strictly to classical Indian ragas, every hymn explores oneness (Ik Onkar), egalitarian community service (Seva), righteous honest labor (Kirat Karo), and divine remembrance (Naam Simran).
fields.cultural_significance: It is reverently treated as a Living Guru rather than a book. It dismantled rigid caste hierarchies, ritualistic dogma, and linguistic discrimination by communicating highest mystical philosophy in the people’s vernaculars set to sublime classical melody.
fields.historical_context: Compiled at Amritsar in 1604 as the Adi Granth and installed at Sri Harmandir Sahib with Baba Buddha as first Granthi. In 1708 at Nanded, the tenth master Guru Gobind Singh commanded: "Sab Sikhan ko hukam hai, Guru manyo Granth."
fields.themes: Divine oneness (Ik Onkar), radical equality, devotion through classical Raga, compassion (Daya), casteless brotherhood, and inner truth (Sat).
fields.available_translations: Complete English translations by Max Arthur Macauliffe, Dr. Gopal Singh, Manmohan Singh, and Sant Singh Khalsa. Available widely on open academic research portals.
fields.custodian_collection: Sri Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple), Amritsar; Takht Sri Hazur Sahib, Nanded; historical Birhs preserved in museum archives.
fields.rights_attribution: Sacred Pan-Indian Heritage. Canonized public spiritual legacy.
fields.excerpt_content:
ੴ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕਰਤਾ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਨਿਰਵੈਰੁ ਅਕਾਲ ਮੂਰਤਿ ਅਜੂਨੀ ਸੈਭੰ ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥
ਜਪੁ ॥ ਆਦਿ ਸਚੁ ਜੁਗਾਦਿ ਸਚੁ ॥ ਹੈ ਭੀ ਸਚੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਹੋਸੀ ਭੀ ਸਚੁ ॥

"There is One Sovereign Supreme Reality, whose name is Eternal Truth;
The Creative Being Personified, Without Fear, Without Enmity,
Timeless Form, Beyond Birth, Self-Existent, Realized by Guru's Grace.
Meditate! True in the Primal Beginning; True throughout the cosmic ages;
True Here and Now; O Nanak, Forever and Ever True."

fields.title: Ramcharitmanas & Valmiki Ramayana (The Epic Traditions)
fields.author_creator: Maharishi Valmiki (Sanskrit Adi-Kavya) & Goswami Tulsidas (Awadhi Ramcharitmanas)
fields.brief_intro: India’s foundational epic explored as an expansive literary tradition with dozens of diverse regional retellings across states and Southeast Asia.
fields.synopsis: Rather than existing as a single monolithic text, the Ramayana is a vibrant civilisational ecosystem. Originating with Maharishi Valmiki’s Sanskrit Adikavya (celebrated for poetic meter Anushtubh), it was retold into Awadhi verse as Ramcharitmanas by Goswami Tulsidas in Varanasi and Ayodhya. It also flourished into Kamban’s Kamba Ramayanam (Tamil 12th c.), Krittibas Ojha’s Krittivasi Ramayan (Bengali 15th c.), Madhava Kandali’s Saptakanda Ramayana (Assamese 14th c.), Ezhuthachan’s Adhyathma Ramayanam Kilippattu (Malayalam 16th c.), and regional folk performance traditions like Ramlila (UNESCO Intangible Heritage).
fields.cultural_significance: The epic shaped moral philosophy, sculpture, puppet theatre (Kathputli, Togalu Gombeyaata), classical dance dramas (Kathakali, Yakshagana), and communal musical sankirtan across every region of India and Southeast Asia (Ramakien in Thailand, Kakawin in Java).
fields.historical_context: Tulsidas began composing the Ramcharitmanas in 1574 CE at Ayodhya on Rama Navami, democratizing spiritual poetry for ordinary commoners who did not know Sanskrit.
fields.themes: Maryada (righteous conduct), filial duty, compassion, democratic retellings, nature and ecology of Dandakaranya, and Bhakti.
fields.available_translations: Freely translated into dozens of global languages, including English verse translations by Ralph T.H. Griffith and modern Gita Press publications.
fields.custodian_collection: Tulsi Mandir, Varanasi; Saraswathi Mahal Library, Thanjavur; National Museum, New Delhi.
fields.rights_attribution: Classical Public Domain & UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage legacy.
fields.excerpt_content:
मंगल भवन अमंगल हारी। द्रवहु सुदसरथ अजिर बिहारी॥
सीय राम मय सब जग जानी। करहुँ प्रनाम जोरि जुग पानी॥

"May that supreme fountain of auspiciousness, which removes all adversity, shower blessing upon all.
Knowing the entire universe to be permeated by Sita and Rama, I bow to all with folded hands in reverence."

fields.title: Thirukkural (The Book of Divine Ethics)
fields.brief_intro: A universal masterwork of 1,330 couplets (Kurals) divided into Virtue (Aram), Wealth (Porul), and Love (Inbam), completely non-denominational and universal in human wisdom.
fields.synopsis: The Thirukkural is universally hailed as one of the greatest moral and philosophical treatises in world literature. Composed by the sage Thiruvalluvar in exactly two-line aphorisms (kural venba), it systematically outlines how human beings should live an upright, compassionate, and meaningful earthly life. Crucially, the work invokes no sectarian deities or supernatural dogma; its ethical imperatives address universal human dignity, hospitality (Virundhombal), truthfulness (Vaimai), avoidance of wrath, statecraft, agricultural dignity, friendship, and reciprocal conjugal love.
fields.cultural_significance: Recognized as the "Universal Veda" (Ulaga Podhumarai). Its ethical tenets guided classical Tamil jurisprudence, inspired Mahatma Gandhi and Leo Tolstoy, and remains a touchstone for humanist moral philosophy.
fields.historical_context: Presented before the Third Tamil Sangam at Madurai. It represents the pinnacle of classical Tamil moral rationality and empirical insight.
fields.themes: Universal ethics, vegetarianism, truthful speech, good governance, mutual respect, hard work, and domestic felicity.
fields.available_translations: Translated into over 42 languages, including the famous 19th-century translation by Rev. G. U. Pope, Father Beschi (Latin), and modern English versions by Rajaji and P. S. Sundaram.
fields.custodian_collection: Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Chennai; Saraswathi Mahal Library, Thanjavur.
